newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's banks seen headed for more record earnings.
newsitem.headline: Canada's banks seen headed for more record earnings.

text.p: Canada's major banks are expected to report higher first-quarter earnings on their way to a fourth straight year of record profits.

"We are expecting earnings for the big six banks to be up about 12 to 13 percent in the first quarter and we're looking for growth in the year to be in the area of eight or nine percent," said Hugh Brown, analyst at brokerage Nesbitt Burns.

Montreal-based National Bank of Canada, the smallest of Canada's big six banks, kicked off the first-quarter earnings parade last week, with earnings for the three months ended Jan. 31 rising to C46 cents (34 cents) a share from year earlier C41 cents (30 cents).
The largest five banks were also expected to post solid first-quarter gains.

Institutional Brokers Estimate System (IBES) said its survey of analysts' projections showed that fourth-ranked Bank of Nova Scotia was expected to show the biggest quarterly gain when it reported results on Tuesday along with third-ranked Bank of Montreal.
Scotiabank's earnings per share were expected to rise C17 cents (13 cents) to C$1.12 (83 cents).
First-quarter earnings at Royal Bank of Canada , Canada's biggest bank, were expected to rise C14 cents (10 cents) a share to C$1.15 (85 cents).

Fifth-ranked Toronto-Dominion Bank's first-quarter earnings per share were seen rising by C11 cents (8 cents) to C81 cents (60 cents), with second-ranked Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce up C10 cents (7.5 cents) to C$1.63 ($1.21) and Bank of Montreal up C7 cents (5 cents) to C$1.11 (82 cents).
Toronto-Dominion Bank was expected to report first-quarter results on Feb. 27, followed by Royal Bank of Canada on March 5 and Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce on March 6.
In fiscal 1996 ended Oct. 31, Canada's big banks posted a double-digit jump in net earnings to a record high C$6.3 billion ($4.7 billion) from C$5.2 billion ($3.8 billion) in 1995.

Analysts said Canadian bank earnings would be driven this year by strong performances in their investment banking, mutual fund and brokerage businesses. Canada's banks dominate regular banking, brokerages and trusts in the country.
The Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's biggest equities market, has hit 10 record highs so far this year.
"The securities business is booming. The mutual fund business is booming. We have a very positive yield curve which is good for bank spreads," said Brown.

Canadian banks were also expected to benefit from increased mortgage lending. Canadian housing starts were seen rising this year as buying interest from first-time buyers began to stir amid interest rates at 40-year lows.
